guide_my_work:
Your personal home: what you have to do today and how your week is going. Everything here is about you only.
Tasks: the tasks assigned to you, due soonest first; open one to update it.
Hours this week: what you logged against your expected hours, so you can see gaps before Friday.
Timer: start it on a task and stop it when you finish; the time goes into your timesheet.
Leave balance: days left per leave type, after approved and requested leave.
guide_team:
The manager's view of the team: who is overloaded, what is late and what is waiting for you.
Workload: hours planned per person against their capacity this week.
Late tasks: tasks past their due date, with the person and project.
Approvals waiting: timesheets, leave and expenses you need to approve or reject.
Utilization: share of billable hours for each person and for the team.
guide_overview:
Company analytics built from your real data: revenue, margin, utilization and cash. Pick a period and compare it with the previous one.
KPI cards: revenue earned, gross margin, utilization and cash collected, with the change against the comparison period.
Revenue over time: earned revenue per week or month against the comparison period.
Revenue by client and revenue bridge: who brings revenue and what made it go up or down.
Clients at risk and team capacity: overdue balances and people near or above 100%.
Report and Victor: download the PDF or CSV report, or ask the assistant a question.
guide_reports:
Standard reports for month-end and for your accountant. Choose a report, set the filters and export.
Report list: timesheet detail, utilization, unbilled hours, invoices, receivables aging, expenses and project profitability.
Filters: period, client, project, employee and department.
Export: Excel (.xlsx), CSV or PDF; the file contains exactly what is on screen.
Cost columns: hidden from people whose role does not allow seeing costs and salaries.
guide_employees:
Everyone who works for the company, with their role, department, rates and status.
List: search and filter by department, role or status; open a person to see their profile.
Add or edit: contact details, job title, manager, contract type, weekly capacity and working days.
Rates: cost rate and billable rate with a start date, so past hours keep the rate of their time.
Status: candidate, active, on leave, notice period or former; former employees keep their history.
guide_org_chart:
Who reports to whom, built from each employee's manager field.
Chart: click a person to fold or unfold their team; the number shows how many people they lead.
Search and department filter: find someone quickly or focus on one department.
Away badges: people on leave today are marked.
guide_documents:
Contracts, IDs and certificates for each employee, with expiry dates. Only HR roles see this page.
Register: every document with its owner, type and expiry status.
Expiry: documents expiring soon or already expired are highlighted; the same alerts appear on the Team dashboard.
Add a document: choose the employee, type, dates and file.
guide_access:
Who can sign in to your company and what they can do. Each login belongs to an employee.
Seats: how many logins your plan allows and how many are used.
Who can sign in: give access, resend the invitation or remove access for each employee.
Role: change it in the list; the role decides the menu and buttons the person sees.
What each role can do: a summary of the rights of admin, manager, accountant, employee and client.
guide_clients:
The companies you work for: billing details, contacts, rates and history.
List: search clients and see their primary contact, account manager and rate.
Add or edit: legal name, ICE, tax ID, addresses, currency, invoice language, payment terms, credit limit and reminders; a warning shows if the client may already exist.
Profile: balance and credit limit, contacts, portal access, contracts, quotes and the activity timeline.
Archive: a client with invoices is archived instead of deleted, so history stays complete.
guide_portal:
Your clients' own space. Decide which client contacts can sign in, and preview what they see.
Who can sign in: give access, resend an invitation or revoke it for each contact; logins unused for 90 days expire.
Preview portal: see exactly what a client sees; approvals are disabled in preview.
What clients get: their projects and milestones, approval of finished milestones, invoices and quotes as PDF, and your bank details.
Client feedback: the portal asks each client to rate approved milestones and finished projects; answers appear on the project, the client profile and the KPI page, and ratings of 2 stars or less reach the project manager's inbox.
guide_portal_client:
Welcome to your portal. Here you follow the work done for you, approve deliverables and get your invoices.
Summary: active projects, items waiting for your approval, your open balance and the next milestone.
Your projects: progress and milestones of each project.
Approve or request changes: when a milestone is finished, approve it or tell the team what should change.
Invoices and quotes: status, amount left to pay and PDF download.
How to pay: bank details; please quote the invoice number when you pay.
Your opinion: after each approved milestone and at the end of a project, rate the work (1 to 5 stars) and say how likely you are to recommend us.
guide_projects:
All projects with their client, budget, progress and health.
List: filter by status, client or health; save the views you use often.
Health: on track, at risk or late, from dates, progress and budget; a manager can override it with a reason.
Budget: hours and money used against the budget, with alerts at 80% and 100%.
Project page: Kanban board, task list, milestones, team, comments and activity.
Budget tab (project page): a budget per phase (milestone) with hours and amount used, and change orders the client approves to raise or lower the budget.
Revenue: on fixed-price projects, revenue earned as the work progresses (hours, tasks or milestones) against what was billed, month by month.
guide_timesheets:
Log the hours you work, per project and task, for each day of the week.
Weekly grid: type hours in 15-minute steps; the total compares with your expected hours.
Timer and quick entry: start a timer on a task, or log recent tasks with large buttons on a phone.
Copy last week: repeat the previous week's rows to save time.
Submit: send the week for approval; approved hours are locked and can then be invoiced.
guide_time_approvals:
Hours your team submitted, waiting for your decision.
Review: see hours per person, project and day.
Approve: one entry, one week or many at once; the rates of the day are saved with the hours.
Reject: give a reason; the person can fix and resubmit.
Reopen: an approved entry that is not invoiced yet can be reopened, and the reopening is logged.
guide_quotes:
Quotes (devis) you send before work starts, from draft to accepted.
List and pipeline: amounts sent, accepted and declined, and quotes about to expire.
Editor: client, lines with quantity and unit, discount, tax, validity and delivery dates.
Send: the quote gets its number and is locked; to change it, duplicate it.
Accepted: turn it into a draft invoice and a fixed-price project in one click; download the PDF any time.
guide_client_invoices:
Invoices to your clients, from draft to paid.
Ready to bill: approved hours not yet invoiced, per client; create an invoice from them.
New invoice: fixed-price share, milestone, retainer, deposit or free lines.
Invoice: issue it (it gets its number and is locked), send it, record payments, or correct it with a credit note.
Statuses: draft, issued, sent, partly paid, paid, overdue or cancelled; download the PDF any time.
guide_recurring_invoices:
Invoices that repeat every month, quarter or year, such as retainers, licences or support.
Schedules: client, lines, tax and rhythm; pause, resume or edit them.
Draft due invoices: create this period's drafts for every schedule that is due.
Review: nothing is issued automatically; check each draft and issue it from Invoices.
guide_receivables:
Money your clients still owe, by how late it is, and the reminders to send.
Aging table: balances per client in not due, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90 and over 90 days.
Payment reminders: overdue invoices ready for their next reminder; preview the message and send it.
Reminder rules: when levels 1, 2 and 3 go out after the due date; turn reminders off for one client in its form.
Export: download the aging table as CSV.
guide_expenses:
Expenses paid by employees or the company, with receipts and approval.
New expense: date, category, amount, tax, project and client, with the receipt above the required amount.
Approval: managers approve or reject; approved expenses are then reimbursed.
Re-bill: mark an expense billable to add it to the client's next invoice.
guide_profitability:
Whether each project makes money: revenue against labour cost and expenses.
Margin per project: revenue, cost of hours (at the rates saved with them), expenses and margin percentage.
Budget use: how much of the budget is spent.
Who sees it: only roles allowed to see costs.
Overhead: when overheads are set in Settings, each logged hour also carries its share of running costs.
guide_timeline:
Every project on one timeline, with milestones and today.
Columns: half months; the current one is highlighted and elapsed time is hatched.
Bars: from start to due date, coloured by health, with progress along the bottom.
Milestones: diamonds on the bar; green once reached.
Navigation: move the window earlier or later, or jump back to today.
guide_calendar:
Deadlines, milestones, leave and holidays on one calendar.
Month view: click a day to see what happens.
Filters: show only one project, team or person.
Colours: deadlines, milestones, approved leave and public holidays each have their own colour.
guide_workload:
How busy each person is, week by week.
Grid: planned hours against capacity, minus leave and holidays.
Colours: above 100% is overloaded, low values mean free time to staff new work.
Use it to: balance work before deadlines slip.
guide_leave:
Leave requests, approvals and balances.
Request: choose the type, dates and half days; the balance is checked before sending.
Approve: managers approve or reject team requests.
Balances: days per type, with carry-over and pro-rating for new hires.
guide_files:
Shared company files and folders.
Upload: drag files in or use the upload button.
Organise: create folders, rename, move and delete.
Preview and download: open images, PDFs and documents in the viewer.
guide_developer:
Keys and webhooks for connecting other software to Nexora.
API keys: create a key with a name and scopes; copy it once, then revoke it when no longer needed.
Usage: requests made with each key.
Keep keys secret: anyone with a key can act with its rights.
guide_settings:
Company settings that every module uses.
Company: legal name, ICE, tax ID, address, currency, fiscal year, logo, document colour and bank details.
Lists: departments, leave types, expense categories, task labels and payment terms.
Approvals: none, one step or two steps for timesheets, leave, expenses, quotes and invoices.
Holidays and period lock: public holidays, and the date up to which nothing can be changed.
Overheads and custom fields: monthly running costs spread over logged hours, and extra fields on clients, projects and employees.
guide_subscription:
Your company's Nexora plan and invoices.
Current plan: price, renewal date and seats used.
Plans: compare and upgrade or downgrade; monthly or yearly (2 months free).
Invoices from Nexora: download each invoice as PDF.
guide_audit_logs:
A permanent record of important changes: who did what and when.
Entries: money, rates, roles, approvals and settings, with the value before and after.
Filters: search by person, action or date.
Records cannot be edited or deleted.

pageDescBankImport: Import your bank statement and turn incoming transfers into invoice payments.
guide_bank_import:
Record client payments from your bank statement instead of typing them one by one.
Upload: the CSV export of your bank (comma or semicolon, dates like 15/10/2026, amounts like 1 234,56). Try the sample statement to see how it works.
Columns: check which column is the date, the label and the amount (one column, or separate credit and debit). Nexora remembers your choice for files with the same layout.
Review: each incoming transfer gets its best invoice, found from the invoice number in the label, the exact amount owed, the client's name and the due date. High means very likely, medium means check it. Pick another invoice, split one transfer over several invoices, or ignore the line. Money going out is not matched.
Confirm: payments are recorded as bank transfers with the bank label as reference; invoices become paid or partly paid. Lines already imported are skipped, so importing a file twice records nothing twice.

guide_today:

Timer: pick a project (and a task) and start; stop to log the time. Only one timer runs at a time.
Today: hours logged today against your daily target (weekly capacity ÷ working days), and the week's total.
Shortcuts: log time in the weekly timesheet, add an expense (with a photo of the receipt), or see your tasks.
Install: on a phone, add Nexora to the home screen (Chrome: Install; iPhone: Share → Add to Home Screen). A long press on the icon offers Start timer, Log time and New expense.
Team view: an admin or manager who is not on any project sees the team's day instead — hours logged today, who logged, running timers and approvals waiting.

guide_staffs:
The Nexora team only: the people who run Nexora, never the people of customer companies.
Roles: each member has one of seven console roles; the Roles page shows what each one may do.
Invite: a link valid 72 hours; two-factor authentication must be set up before the first console page.
Change or remove: every change is confirmed (owners also type a code from their authenticator app) and written to the audit trail. Removing someone ends their sessions at once. The team always keeps at least one platform owner.
guide_roles:
What each console role may do, from the cahier des charges (Table 23). The table is read-only: roles are fixed and the server applies the same rules.
Columns: the seven roles, with how many team members hold each; your own role is highlighted.
Badges: Yes; Yes + 2FA (a fresh authenticator code at the moment of the action); 2FA + 2nd person (another member approves); Staff only (admins manage members but not owners).
Customer data: no role reads a company's business data; only support sessions approved by the company give access.
guide_sessions:
Every console sign-in of the Nexora team, so a lost laptop or a strange location can be cut off at once.
Limits: a session ends after 30 minutes without activity or 12 hours in total; then two-factor sign-in is needed again.
End session: owners, admins and engineers can end anyone's session; everyone can end their own. The person is signed out at once and the action is written to the audit trail.
Abroad: sign-ins from outside Morocco are counted so the owner can check them.
guide_platform_audit:
Every console action that changed money, access, status or configuration: who, with which role, on what, before and after, when, and from which IP and session.
Filters: by person, action and period, or search a name or value.
Export: platform owners only, after a code from their authenticator app; the export itself becomes an event.
Rules: events are append-only, nobody can edit or delete them, and they are kept 5 years. Support sessions will appear here and in the customer's own audit log.
